```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence is stronger and more specific. Three independent, sourced quotes describe recurring, costly pain: one founder hired someone despite the cost, another cites a quantified 3-4 hours per month of reconciliation, and a third names concrete failure modes such as revenue recognition, fees, refunds and failed payments. A has only two demand quotes, and one of them is a complaint that $50-80/mo is too much to pay.",
    "B has a sourced, low-cost, targeted channel. The Stripe App Marketplace puts the product directly in front of the exact users whose Stripe-to-bank pain it solves. A relies on Google Ads at a sourced $5.42 average CPC and on Product Hunt, whose own cited anecdote shows highly variable results, while competing with dozens of similar launches.",
    "A's saturation is documented as more extreme. A pricing study covers 73 comparable tools, 50% offer a free plan and entry pricing has converged around $29/mo. B faces 6+ competitors, which is crowded but a smaller field, and a narrow wedge such as pure Stripe-bank reconciliation is identified.",
    "A's own brief includes sourced marketer commentary that generic feedback tools get ignored. That undercuts the chance of landing a first paying customer within 90 days without a sharp wedge, and the brief does not identify one.",
    "B's mechanical, rules-based reconciliation task fits agent automation well. Sourced competitor pricing of $29-100/mo shows self-serve buyers pay for it."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence is thin and partly cuts against the idea. The pain quote comes from a post by a builder promoting their own competing widget, not from a prospective buyer. The only buyer-side quote, 'Spending $50-80/month on a feedback widget is ridiculous,' signals price resistance rather than willingness to pay. No source shows a buyer actively looking to switch or to pay for a new tool.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated categories with free-tier competitors, and neither identifies a proven wedge. B carries a heavier trust and compliance burden: SOC2 is described as commercially expected, Plaid and Stripe terms need legal review, and its privacy-compliance claim is marked [unsourced], all of which could slow a first sale. B's $400-600/mo Growthy bookkeeper-cost figure has no link and is treated as missing. The choice rests mainly on B's stronger buyer-pain evidence and its targeted Stripe Marketplace channel, not on a clear market opening."
}
```
